# Finding ∫ -3x⁴ sin(x) dx

This requires repeated integration by parts. I'll use the tabular method on ∫ x⁴ sin(x) dx first, then multiply by -3.

## Tabular Integration by Parts for ∫ x⁴ sin(x) dx

| Sign | Differentiate | Integrate |
|------|--------------|-----------|
| + | x⁴ | sin(x) |
| − | 4x³ | −cos(x) |
| + | 12x² | −sin(x) |
| − | 24x | cos(x) |
| + | 24 | sin(x) |

Multiplying along the diagonals:

$$\int x^4 \sin(x)\,dx = -x^4\cos(x) + 4x^3\sin(x) + 12x^2\cos(x) - 24x\sin(x) - 24\cos(x) + C$$

## Multiply by −3:

$$\int -3x^4 \sin(x)\,dx = 3x^4\cos(x) - 12x^3\sin(x) - 36x^2\cos(x) + 72x\sin(x) + 72\cos(x) + C$$

## Verification (differentiate the result):

- d/dx[3x⁴cos(x)] = 12x³cos(x) − 3x⁴sin(x)
- d/dx[−12x³sin(x)] = −36x²sin(x) − 12x³cos(x)
- d/dx[−36x²cos(x)] = −72xcos(x) + 36x²sin(x)
- d/dx[72xsin(x)] = 72sin(x) + 72xcos(x)
- d/dx[72cos(x)] = −72sin(x)

All terms cancel except **−3x⁴sin(x)** ✓

<answer>3*x**4*cos(x) - 12*x**3*sin(x) - 36*x**2*cos(x) + 72*x*sin(x) + 72*cos(x) + C</answer>
